sections.title: باب 6 — متن (8)

If the hands or arms strike the ball with stiffness, then as a result of the action a reaction will arise in the opposite direction, and the ball will go back towards the opposite court, through which the team receiving the service will lose the chance of attack.

sections.theory:
… should be given, and the hands and arms should be kept loose. If the hands or arms strike the ball with stiffness, then as a result of the action a reaction will arise in the opposite direction, and the ball will go back towards the opposite court, through which the team receiving the service will lose the chance of attack.

Biomechanical principles in the action of Boosting

Boosting is the action of preparing the ball for the smash. In other words, tossing the ball near the net for the smash is called boosting. As soon as the ball comes over the head of the booster, the booster, making the shape of a cup with his fingers, lifts the ball up over the net. In this action too Newton’s laws apply.

Smashing and biomechanical principles

In the action of smashing, jumping and hitting the ball are included. To jump and hit the ball, the player, bringing his centre of gravity (Center of Gravity) down, initially spends force on the surface of the ground and jumps and smashes the ball, and according to the third law of motion, as much force as he spends on the ball, as a reaction the ball will go towards the other court. The player, while jumping and coming back to the ground, will also maintain his balance.
